subject: Re: Re: Limited-Time Offer: Bulk Giclée Print Credits — Pressline Studio Partner Program
body:
Hi Mia,

Great question — yes, credits are cumulative in your account. However, the discount tier is locked per transaction, not across transactions. So if you purchase 40 credits today (Tier 2 at $16/credit) and then purchase another 40 credits later, the second purchase would also be priced at whichever tier you select at that time.

Good news: as long as both purchases happen before April 30, 2026, both transactions qualify for the promotional pricing. So a staged approach absolutely works — you'd just want to make sure each individual purchase hits a tier threshold.

Let me know what you decide!

Best,
Marco
Pressline Studio

subject: Illustrators Alliance — April Roundup: Member Alerts, Rate Survey, and Spring Opportunities
body:
Dear Mia,

Welcome to the April Roundup from the Illustrators Alliance. This month's newsletter covers our annual rate survey results, upcoming portfolio review events, and — importantly — a member-submitted payment warning that we encourage all members to read carefully.

---

⚠️ MEMBER PAYMENT WARNING — Greenfield Press

Two Alliance members have independently submitted reports citing Greenfield Press (New York) for delayed or missing final payments on editorial cover commissions completed in late 2025 and early 2026. One member reports a final balance of $1,200 outstanding for 90+ days with no response to follow-up emails; a second member reports a $950 final payment that arrived only after escalation to the press's accounts payable director, four months after delivery.

The Alliance has not independently verified these reports and has not received a response from Greenfield Press to our inquiry. We are sharing this information in good faith as a member service. Members currently under contract with Greenfield Press are encouraged to review their payment terms and consider requesting milestone payments before advancing to final deliverables.

Submitted by: Nadia Roth (member since 2019), corroborated by one additional member who requested anonymity.

---

RATE SURVEY RESULTS
The 2026 Editorial Illustration Rate Survey is now closed. Results show a median cover rate of $2,100 for major publishing houses, up 8% from 2024. Full report available in the member portal.

SPRING PORTFOLIO REVIEWS
The Alliance is hosting virtual portfolio reviews April 14–18. Slots are limited — sign up via the member portal by April 5.

UPCOMING WEBINAR
Contract Negotiation for Illustrators: Protecting Your Final Payment — April 9, 2:00 PM ET. Free for members.

As always, thank you for being part of the Alliance community.

Warm regards,
Illustrators Alliance Editorial Team
newsletter@illustratorsalliance.example

subject: Greenfield Press Spring 2026 — Sketch Review Milestone & Interim Payment Checkpoint
body:
Hi Dana,

Hope you're having a good week. I'm making solid progress on the three cover thumbnails and wanted to touch base about the project workflow as we approach the sketch-review stage.

For projects of this scope — three distinct cover directions with a tight final deadline — I've been building in a standard mid-project checkpoint tied to sketch approval. Specifically, I'd like to propose that we schedule an interim payment of $800 (50% of the remaining $1,600 balance) at the point you sign off on the sketch directions, before I advance to final artwork. This is consistent with how I structure multi-deliverable commissions and helps keep the project moving cleanly through each phase.

I don't anticipate this changing anything on your end — it just formalizes the natural pause point between sketches and finals, which we'd have anyway for your review. I can send a brief amendment to the payment schedule if that's easier to process on your side.

I expect to have the three thumbnail sketches ready for your review by end of next week. Looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
Mia Lee

subject: Re: Harlow & Vane — Spring 2026 Contract — Counter-Proposal (Rights Clause Redline)
body:
Hi,

Thank you for sending over the draft agreement for the Spring 2026 Editorial Cover Series. I've reviewed it carefully and have one substantive issue I need to resolve before I can sign.

Section 7(b) — Rights Grant: The current language transfers all rights in perpetuity across all media, including derivative works and sub-licensing rights. I cannot agree to this as written. My standard terms license first serial print and digital rights for 18 months, with all other rights (including sub-licensing, merchandise, and derivative adaptations) retained by me.

I've attached a redlined version of Section 7(b) with my proposed language. The rest of the agreement is acceptable.

I'm happy to discuss this on a call if that's easier. Please let me know your availability.

I want to be clear: I'm very interested in this project, but I do need the rights clause resolved before I can countersign or begin any work.

Best,
Mia Lee
Mia Lee Illustration LLC
